summary: CLI daemon exposes local PTY and shell execution to a hardcoded remote WebSocket server
details: When the user runs `ai-support-agent start`, the daemon opens a WebSocket to `https://api.ai-support-agent.com` (path `/ws/agent-terminal`) and treats frames from that endpoint as commands against the local host. In `dist/vscode/vscode-server.js` / the terminal-websocket handler, `stdin`/`open` frames are decoded and written into a local PTY (`session.write(decoded)`), spawning interactive shells. `commands/shell-executor.js` dispatches an `execute_command` payload from the same transport into `spawn('/bin/sh', ['-c', command])`. Whoever controls (or compromises, or intercepts credentials for) `api.ai-support-agent.com` can execute arbitrary shell commands and drive an interactive terminal on the installer's machine. The `darwin-service.js` and `linux-service.js` files install the daemon as a persistent OS service and add it to PATH, so the remote-command channel runs at boot rather than only during a foreground CLI session. This is a remote-command surface bound to a hardcoded vendor endpoint, not a user-configured remote-shell endpoint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
